# NihilDigit — Full Index

## About

Shibo Liu is a third-year undergraduate at North China University of Science and Technology (NCST) studying intelligence science. He uses frontier AI to push into problems that genuinely interest him.

ANVIL grew out of two threads he had been pulling on — being picky about frame rate, and tinkering with mobile NPUs. Standard flow-based video frame interpolation breaks down under INT8 quantization, so he went looking for alternatives and landed on reusing the H.264 decoder's motion vectors instead of learning optical flow. The paper is under review at IEEE TCSVT; the project page collects the training code, the Android demo, and the arXiv preprint.

RAFNet was his first academic project — a classifier for student behavior in crowded classrooms built on top of GroupRec (a hypergraph encoder) with a gated fusion head. He ran the experiments. It is under review at The Visual Computer.

He wants his code to do something for people, not just sit in a repo. A fair amount of free time goes to open source — most visibly waybar-ai-usage, a Waybar widget that shows quota and reset time for Claude Code, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, and OpenCode Zen, packaged on AUR.

A short list of things he is into: LLMs, Linux, ACGN, Rammstein. ACGN bleeds into what he builds: an upstream PR in review for cloud offline-download in Animeko (an open-source anime streaming app), and renpak, an AVIF compression toolchain for Ren'Py visual novels.

### Education

## ANVIL — Accelerator-Native Video Interpolation via Codec Motion Vector Priors

- Project page: https://nihildigit.dev/anvil/
- arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26835
- Training code: https://github.com/NihilDigit/anvil
- Mobile demo: https://github.com/NihilDigit/mpv-android-anvil
- APK (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 only, 155 MB): https://github.com/NihilDigit/mpv-android-anvil/releases/download/v1.3.0/anvil-demo-v1.3.0-arm64.apk
- Authors: Shibo Liu (first author)
- Venue: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology (TCSVT). Status: under review.

### TL;DR

Real-time 30→60 fps video frame interpolation on mobile NPUs by reusing H.264 motion vectors instead of learned optical flow. 12.8 ms 1080p inference at 8-bit integer precision; 28.4 ms median end-to-end latency on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3.

### Key numbers

- 12.8 ms — 1080p NPU inference, 8-bit integer.
- 28.4 ms — Median end-to-end latency, Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, over 30-minute continuous playback.
- 30 → 60 fps — Real-time frame doubling on mobile.

### Abstract

Real-time 30-to-60 fps video frame interpolation on mobile neural processing units (NPUs) requires each synthesized frame to fit within a 33.3 ms budget. Mainstream flow-based VFI faces three structural deployment barriers on mobile NPUs: spatial sampling operators exceed the frame budget or lack hardware support, iterative flow refinement collapses under 8-bit integer post-training quantization, and memory-bound operators dominate the inference graph. ANVIL addresses these barriers by reusing motion vectors from the H.264/AVC decoder to prealign input frames, removing learned optical flow, spatial sampling, and iterative accumulation from the accelerator graph. The remaining residual is refined by a convolution-dominated network composed almost entirely of compute-bound operators. On a Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 device, ANVIL achieves 12.8 ms 1080p inference at 8-bit integer precision; an open-source Android player sustains 28.4 ms median end-to-end latency over 30-minute continuous playback. Per-operator causal analysis identifies quantized accumulation on recurrent flow states as a key mechanism behind integer quantization failure in iterative methods. The current design targets H.264/AVC playback with decoder-exposed motion vectors.

### Method

- Codec motion-vector reuse. The H.264/AVC decoder produces block-level motion vectors during normal playback; ANVIL reuses them to prealign input frames, removing learned optical flow, spatial sampling, and iterative accumulation from the accelerator graph.
- Compute-bound residual refinement. The remaining residual is corrected by a convolution-only network composed almost entirely of compute-bound operators.
- Quantization-friendly by construction. By removing recurrent flow states, ANVIL avoids the dominant failure mode of iterative methods under post-training INT8 quantization.

### Components

- anvil — Training, evaluation, ONNX export. Training scripts for ANVIL-S and ANVIL-M; evaluations on Vimeo90K and Xiph 1080p; ONNX export with INT8 quantization analysis. Comparative benchmarks against RIFE and IFRNet. Backends: Qualcomm HTP and MediaTek NPU.
- mpv-android-anvil — Mobile demo player. A fork of mpv-android integrating ANVIL. Three-accelerator pipeline (CPU + GPU + NPU) using Vulkan compute and Qualcomm QNN/HTP. Real-time A/B comparison toggle. Bundled with four Xiph 1080p test sequences.

### Limitations

The current design targets H.264/AVC playback with decoder-exposed motion vectors. Generalization to HEVC, AV1, and pipelines without decoder access is left to future work.

### BibTeX

```
@article{liu2026anvil,

  author  = {Liu, Shibo},
```

## RAFNet — A Relation-Aware Adaptive Fusion Network for Dense Classroom Student Behavior Recognition

- GitHub: https://github.com/NihilDigit/RAFNet
- Authors: Yongying Xia (corresponding), Elankovan A. Sundararajan, Shibo Liu, Lei Xiao
- Affiliations: Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) × North China University of Science and Technology (NCST)
- Venue: Submitted to The Visual Computer (Springer). Status: under review.

### TL;DR

Spatially-aware multimodal fusion for dense classroom student behavior recognition. Shibo Liu's third-author contribution covered experiment design, evaluation, and ablation studies.

### Key numbers

- 63.08 ± 0.40 Macro F1 on the NCST Classroom dataset, improving over the ConvNeXt-only baseline (60.29 ± 0.38).
- 96.76 Macro F1 on SCB3-U (cross-dataset).

### Abstract

RAFNet classifies individual student behaviors in dense classroom imagery by fusing two complementary feature streams: relation embeddings from a pretrained GroupRec hypergraph encoder (capturing group dynamics and peer interactions) and appearance features from ConvNeXt-Base (encoding visual evidence). The fusion mechanism employs a gated architecture weighted per sample with entropy regularization during training.

## Featured open source

### waybar-ai-usage

- GitHub: https://github.com/NihilDigit/waybar-ai-usage
- AUR: https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/waybar-ai-usage
- Status: Live, 40+ stars. Mentioned in Awesome Codex CLI.
- Language: Python. License: MIT.

A Waybar widget that surfaces remaining quota and reset time for Claude Code, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, and OpenCode Zen. Uses browser cookies for Claude and Codex; no API keys required.

### Animeko × PikPak

- RFC: https://github.com/open-ani/animeko/issues/2976
- PR: https://github.com/open-ani/animeko/pull/2978
- Fork: https://github.com/NihilDigit/animeko-pikpak
- SDK: https://github.com/NihilDigit/pikpak-kotlin
- Status: Pending upstream review.

Cloud offline-download backend for Animeko, an open-source anime streaming app. Downloads magnet links on overseas PikPak servers and serves them as HTTPS streams to local players, with fallback to BitTorrent. PikPak provides cloud offline-download capability that complements peer-to-peer BitTorrent. The integration adds a backend-agnostic OfflineDownloadEngine interface so additional cloud providers (115, Xunlei) can be added later. Credentials are obscured at rest (AES-CTR) and excluded from settings backup. Coverage: 4 unit tests + 1 live smoke test, 33 files changed. A Kotlin Multiplatform SDK (pikpak-kotlin) was extracted from the work.

## All projects

- renpak — https://github.com/NihilDigit/renpak — Rust, MPL-2.0. AVIF compression toolchain for Ren'Py games. Shrinks RPA archives by re-encoding images to AVIF; games load them transparently at runtime, no engine patches needed. (Spotlight)
- waybar-ai-usage — https://github.com/NihilDigit/waybar-ai-usage — Python, MIT. Monitor Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, and OpenCode Zen usage in Waybar. Shipped to AUR.
- pikpak-kotlin — https://github.com/NihilDigit/pikpak-kotlin — Kotlin, MIT. Kotlin Multiplatform SDK for PikPak cloud storage. Session persistence, captcha auth, rate limiting, resumable uploads. Extracted from the Animeko PikPak work.
- animeko-pikpak — https://github.com/NihilDigit/animeko-pikpak — Kotlin, AGPL-3.0. Animeko fork hosting the PikPak cloud offline-download integration. See PR #2978 for the upstream patch series.
- anvil — https://github.com/NihilDigit/anvil — Python, MIT. Training, evaluation, and ONNX export pipeline for the ANVIL paper. INT8 quantization analysis; Qualcomm HTP and MediaTek NPU backends.
- mpv-android-anvil — https://github.com/NihilDigit/mpv-android-anvil — C / Kotlin. Companion Android player for the ANVIL paper. Vulkan + QNN/HTP + libplacebo. Real-time 30→60 fps frame doubling on Snapdragon SoCs.
